title: Tandem Canopy Piloting Proficiency
description: Recall flashcards from user-supplied course-material images; not official exam questions.
sourcePolicy: Source_verified means faithful to the supplied image, not independent verification against every current manual. Older procedures and unattributed checklist values must not silently override newer manufacturer guidance.

usage.grading: Self-assess recall cards; do not require correctOptionId. Use includeInQuiz for default scored practice; review excluded cards separately.
usage.practice: Rehearse EP handle sequences with the examiner in a training harness. Canopy drills are supervised course exercises.

cards.question: What are the three-flare drills and objective?
cards.answer: Find first-stage flare sweet spot: identify tandem pair penduluming under canopy nose; two-stage flare looking forward; repeat two-stage flare with eyes closed.
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.

cards.question: What are the flare-familiarity drills?
cards.answer: Full brakes 8–10 seconds then full flight and observe flight cycle; 90-degree turn with quick return to full flight, then another with slow return; observe each cycle.
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.

cards.question: What are the braked-flare drills?
cards.answer: Hold quarter, half, and three-quarter brakes for 5 seconds each, then perform a dynamic flare from each setting.
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.

cards.question: What are the rear-riser familiarity drills?
cards.answer: 90-degree right/left turns with brakes stowed; repeat unstowed; with brakes unstowed try a rear-riser flare grasping above guide rings and symmetrically pulling approximately 6–8 inches.
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.

cards.question: What is the forced-recovery drill?
cards.answer: Aggressive 90–180-degree turn; neutralize turn then immediately symmetric flare, “match & finish”; repeat opposite direction. Objective: simulate collision/obstacle avoidance.
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.

cards.question: What is the repositioning-over-ground drill?
cards.answer: Hold three-quarter brakes; while in deep brakes turn 90 right, 90 left, 90 left, 90 right to original heading. Also called sashay, S-turn, or quad 90s; objective mid-pattern repositioning for accuracy.
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.

cards.question: What is the flat-turn-to-flare drill?
cards.answer: 45-degree flat turns followed by a flare after each turn; objective obstacle avoidance.
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.

cards.question: How do you assess altitude loss in turns?
cards.answer: 360-degree full-input turn then full flight, note altitude loss; repeat with quarter input, note altitude loss.
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.

cards.question: What stacking and communication exercises are listed?
cards.answer: Compare descent rates; use half brakes to increase vertical separation; pass on-level canopies using full-input turns; ideally establish canopy order by 2,000 feet/600 meters.
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.

cards.question: How are running, holding, and crabbing assessed?
cards.answer: Fly full flight and look down body line to assess ground track; determine heading angle needed for lateral ground track (crabbing).
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.

cards.question: How may examiners organize or combine drills?
cards.answer: Jumps may occur in any order for weather, run-in/release issues, and DZ deconfliction; examiners have creative control; exercises can be combined if altitude permits; candidate can pull slightly higher for additional drill altitude.
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.

cards.question: What preparation and accuracy requirements are listed?
cards.answer: Rehearse canopy dive flows on ground before jumping; landing accuracy as directed in Tandem Instructor Logbook.
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.

cards.question: What if safety concerns or unforeseen circumstances prevent drill completion?
cards.answer: No repeat jumps necessary, but candidates are encouraged to complete all drills before final endorsement. Safety first.
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.

cards.question: What if the candidate is under a reserve?
cards.answer: Concentrate solely on landing priorities and dismiss the briefed canopy dive flow.
cards.explanation: Answer transcribed or paraphrased from the named course material.
